output.headline: Warburg Pincus has bought three Health IT companies and has an open platform for an add-on; the $300M price sits within its returns.
output.differentiator: Matches Blackstone and TPG on three deals in the target's sub-sector and an open platform. Only TPG has more National-region deals than its three, so its footprint matches the target's.
output.why_them: Add-on to open Health IT platform; three sub-sector deals

acquirer_overview.title: A growth investor with a sub-sector record, though most deals lie elsewhere
points: 23 deals from 2016 to 2024, 16 closed (70%); 21 of 23 were control deals rather than minority stakes [K:closed_share, K:control_share].
Over $100 billion in assets under management, and 22 private equity funds raised, so capital is not the constraint [P:1, P:3].
Home sub-sector is Home Health/Hospice; only 3 of 23 deals were in Health IT, and 20 were outside it [B:buyer, T:record].

strategic_fit_thesis.title: A Health IT add-on for an open platform, backed by a growth motive
points: Three deals in the target's own sub-sector, and an open platform there makes the target an add-on route [T:record, A:angles].
Growth was a motive in 11 of 23 deals, which suits the target's 20.0% revenue growth [M:high_growth].
Platform Build appears in 5 of 23 deals, in line with the file overall; activity, regional fit and deal size are only slight factors for it [M:platform_build, S:activity, S:geo_fit, S:not_smaller].

precedent_activity.title: Three Health IT deals, all closed, at 19.4x to 25.7x EBITDA
points: Apex EHR Solutions ($186M, 2023, Platform Investment) at 25.7x, and Universal Health AI ($219M, 2022, Management Buyout) at 23.3x [D:MA-2023-0481, D:MA-2022-0252].
Keystone EHR Solutions ($382M, 2021, Platform Investment) at 19.4x, the largest of the three and above the target's $300M [D:MA-2021-0441].
8 of 23 deals sit in the $150M-$600M comparable size band, and 7 have come since 2022 [K:size_band, K:recent].

valuation_context.title: The 50th percentile is defensible, and the returns clear the hurdle
points: 13 comparable deals price at 19.4x to 23.3x, median 21.4x; the 25.0% margin beats the comps' 22.2% median, so the 50th percentile holds [V:comps].
Its overall median paid is 15.6x, below the comps, yet its three Health IT deals cleared 19.4x to 25.7x [T:record, D:MA-2023-0481, D:MA-2021-0441].
At 5.0x leverage and 8.5% interest, a $239M equity cheque returns 25.3% IRR at the ask against a 20% target; maximum price is $356M [V:lbo].

risk_flags.title: Size stretch
risk_flags.concern: Median deal of $106M is under half the $300M EV [T:record].
risk_flags.mitigant: Its Health IT deals ran from $186M to $382M, and 8 of 23 deals sit in the size band [D:MA-2023-0481, D:MA-2021-0441, K:size_band].
risk_flags.reality: The stretch is against its typical deal, not its Health IT record; its biggest deal was $2,124M [T:record].

risk_flags.title: Closing record
risk_flags.concern: Only 16 of 23 deals closed (70%), a modest factor against it [K:closed_share, S:close_rate_s].
risk_flags.mitigant: All three Health IT precedents closed [D:MA-2023-0481, D:MA-2022-0252, D:MA-2021-0441].
risk_flags.reality: Both withdrawn deals among its listed precedents were in neighbouring sectors, not Health IT [D:MA-2020-0201, D:MA-2018-0413].

risk_flags.title: Competitive process and price
risk_flags.concern: Seventh on a priority list of 10; Blackstone and Evolent Health also rate High [R:rank].
risk_flags.mitigant: IRR of 25.3% at the ask clears the 20% target, leaving room to bid [V:lbo].
risk_flags.reality: Its 15.6x median paid is below the 21.4x comps median, so it must pay above habit [T:record, V:comps].

conviction.rationale: Three deals in the target's own sub-sector and an open platform support an add-on route, but its median deal of $106M is under half the $300M EV. [C:conviction, T:record, A:angles]
